statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Weekend venue closure with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail remains far below the block threshold while Stress stays elevated on hawkish rate repricing and Hormuz energy risk.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the session; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Closed weekend tape: hawkish payroll repricing and a second day of Hormuz escalation meet a thin Sunday reopen
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape is Friday September 4: ^NDX closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, and VIX ended at 14.53. The S&P 500 closed 7,718.41 (-0.38%) and the Nasdaq Composite 26,506.99 (-0.29%) after the August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 53,000 consensus. That lifted the 2-year Treasury to 4.377%, its highest since January 2025, and the 10-year to about 4.784%, while CME FedWatch pricing for a 25bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC rose to 58.4% from 49.4% a day earlier. H.15 still shows September 3 readings of 4.34% and 4.77%. The US-Iran conflict escalated again on Saturday: after the IRGC fired ballistic missiles toward a US carrier and destroyer, CENTCOM disabled or destroyed three Iranian crude tankers, and the IRGC then claimed strikes on three US-affiliated vessels and three tankers in Hormuz. Brent ended the week near $96.28 and WTI near $91.48, Brent's strongest week since mid-July, with only four commodity vessels transiting the strait on Thursday against a ten-day average near 15. That combination keeps Stress elevated. The strategy-relevant failure mode, however, requires an observed no-retracement price path, and none exists: Friday closed mid-range, VIX stayed below 15, and cross-asset signals conflict rather than align. Tail therefore stays low and maps to EA_ON. Conditional risk concentrates in the 22:00-02:00 UTC reopen window, where the thinnest depth of the week meets a Monday US holiday that removes the cash session normally available to absorb a weekend gap.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held flat at 4-5 with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress climbed from 38 during Friday's European session to a 57 peak around the U.S. close as the payroll beat lifted yields, then oscillated between 52 and 56 across the weekend closure. Dominant mode stayed normal for every hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover 13 further closed hours, the 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian session on a US Labor Day holiday. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band throughout, peaking at 18 in the reopen hour where two verified days of Hormuz escalation meet the thinnest depth of the week, then decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 66 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop. No US macro release falls inside the window; the next scheduled checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
